source: Book V printed pp.38-39 = book5-6.pdf PDF pp.44-45; rule printed p.38 (PDF p.44), program, circuit diagram and procedure p.39 (PDF p.45); wires image-read on PDF p.45; Step 7 speculative derivation from topology
note: Speculative (Step 7): every expect is derived by hand from the wiring and the p.38 rule P X E = their, E X P(not) = her; the page prints only the lamp meanings, not which lights come on for any input (programs.json printedUnprinted). Topology: + feeds the arms 2Y and 3Y. Pushbutton 2's N.O. 2X drives 3C: light 3 ('Pete', 3A-3B/3-) and relay 3 (3C-indicator-3E-coil-3F/3B/3-). Pushbutton 3's N.O. 3X drives 1Y and 4A: light 4 ('Eve', 4B/4-) and pushbutton 1's arm. Pushbutton 1's N.O. 1X feeds relay 3's set-1 arm 3H: N.O. 3G to light 1 ('their'), N.C. 3J to light 2 ('her'). So light 1 = pb1 AND pb3 AND pb2, light 2 = pb1 AND pb3 AND NOT pb2; 'ihrem' with Piet alone lights neither. No contact feeds a coil, so there is no latch. Script follows the page's procedure (select the subject with pushbuttons 2 and/or 3, then push pushbutton 1), covering Piet, Eva, Piet and Eva, the Piet release with ihrem held, and ihrem alone. The 500 ms advance before each expect lets lamps finish their thermal transient; the page states no timing. No errata apply.

script.quote: The basic rule which we must teach the computer is: a plural subject requires the use of "their" as an adjective; a singular feminine subject requires the use of "her" as an adjective. This can be stated logically as: P X E = their and E X P̄ = her
